thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: elevated packet loss observed from multiple edge POPs in us-east3 — aggregated egress loss > 12% over the last 5m. Auto-escalating to #incidents and paging oncall.

diego.ops: I'm on it. seeing a flurry of BGP withdraws from provider A toward our us-east3 edge layer. first spike at ~5m ago, sustained. some prefixes flapping.

irene.sre: thanks. are customer origin/backhaul links affected or just CDN-to-edge? what's the impact on origin fetches vs client e2e?

diego.ops: initial telemetry: client->edge packet loss high (SYN retransmits), edge->origin slightly degraded for a subset of hosts. last-mile for some ISPs looks fine — issue correlates with provider A transit in the region.

maya.prod: multiple customer pings reporting 504s and slow streaming. support queue rising. pushing notice to status page: "degraded CDN performance in us-east region". (drafted)

samir.net: looking at BGP table — peer 203.0.113.10 is withdrawing our next-hops to several /24s intermittently. MTR traces show consistent loss at their ASN path. suspecting provider side evictions.

diego.ops: running mitigation steps:
1) shifting traffic weight away from us-east3 -> us-east1/us-east2 via edge-pop weight override in control plane (will take ~30s to propagate).
2) enabling aggressive origin fallback to nearest healthy POP for streaming routes.
3) opening ticket with provider A NOC, sending collected bgp logs + timestamps.

irene.sre: please post the control-plane commands you used and the rollback plan.

diego.ops: command used (control plane):

```
redwood-edgectl set-pop-weight --region us-east3 --weight 0.2 --reason "emerg: providerA BGP flapping"
redwood-edgectl set-pop-weight --region us-east1 --weight 0.5
redwood-edgectl set-pop-weight --region us-east2 --weight 0.3
```

Rollback plan: revert weights to previous values if packet loss subsides below 1% for 3 consecutive 5m windows, or if provider confirms fix.

samir.net: added BGP adj logs to ticket. ticket# 987654 with provider A created. Provider NOC responded: "we see flapping, investigating fiber splice/aggregate device". ETA unknown.

liz.support: fielding customer escalations. top affected customers: AcmeCorp (streaming), FinCart (API bursts). Making playbook entries: credit threshold + inbound ticket templates.

maya.prod: status page update posted, TTL 60s, included mitigation note and next update in 30m.

diego.ops: traffic shift in flight — monitoring client-side error rates. initial telemetry: 60% of impacted traffic already shifted to other POPs. error rates dropping but still above baseline for some prefixes.

irene.sre: start incident severity assessment: impact = partial regional degradation for CDN egress in us-east3, estimated customer-visible errors 7-12%, escalation to P1 due to SLO breach for streaming customers. paging execs.

incident-bot: :pager: P1 incident created: INC-2026-4323. Handoff channel: #incidents-INC-2026-4323. All updates sync there.

samir.net: small routing tweak attempt: re-advertised more specific /24s from fallback ASNs to prefer healthy paths. Need to watch for route churn.

diego.ops: observed transient route dampening on provider A after we pulled weight. keeping dampening off on our side. asking edge infra to raise conn tracking limits temporarily.

maya.prod: customer communications: queued targeted emails to top 5 paying customers, including instructions to switch to multi-pop endpoints (we have a geo-failover header). send now?

liz.support: sending now. included apology, ETA unknown, mitigation steps, support contact.

irene.sre: oncall handoff in 30m — @samir.net will take next shift. Diego, please leave a runbook snippet for further actions.

samir.net: noted. plan while oncall: continue BGP monitoring, coordinate with provider NOC, keep traffic weights adjusted, prepare to initiate origin-level cache priming if we see origin amplification.

diego.ops: runbook snippet added to incident doc: "if provider fixes announced, gradually restore pop weight: increment us-east3 by +0.2 every 5m while observing loss, do not exceed historical baseline; if loss persists, engage legal for possible transit contract clause." :grimacing:

irene.sre: any DNS changes considered? lowering TTL for CNAME steering could help, but majority is routing-level. Avoid wide DNS churn unless provider indicates long outage.

samir.net: provider updated: potential fiber splice issue. they propose traffic engineering on their side in 10-15m. will monitor BGP stability post-engineering.

diego.ops: metrics: before mitigation client-side 5xx rate in us-east3 = 11%. after weight shift -> down to 3.2% currently. still seeing sporadic 502 bursts to streaming endpoints.

maya.prod: support queues dropping slightly. keep status updates every 15m.

liz.support: customer AcmeCorp responded, says failover improved playback but some cached assets still error; suggested we purge CDN edge for that customer. any objections?

diego.ops: go ahead with targeted purge for AcmeCorp on the POPs they've been hitting. command:

```
redwood-cdn purge --customer acmecorp --pops us-east1,us-east2
```

samir.net: provider reports their TE completed. BGP table shows no new withdraws for 3m. loss trending down.

irene.sre: revert plan: if stability holds for 15m, start gradual restore of pop weights. ensure we document exact restore times and telemetry windows.

diego.ops: starting weight restoration in 2m: lowering us-east1 to 0.4, us-east2 to 0.35, us-east3 to 0.25.

incident-bot: Note: automatic postmortem scheduled in 24h; assign to oncall handoff owner (samir.net).

samir.net: taking postmortem ownership. will collect BGP dumps, provider comms, traffic-shift logs.

maya.prod: closing incident chat soon? want to keep thread pinned until postmortem.

irene.sre: keep pinned and set meeting for 1h after incident for quick RCA sync. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

diego.ops: handing off to @samir.net. I'm available if provider asks for additional logs.

samir.net: received handoff — monitoring. updating the ticket and incident doc.

liz.support: final note: confirmed top-5 customers all notified and support actions taken. will follow up with refunds/credits per SLA.

incident-bot: Incident status: mitigated -> observable stability. Will move to monitoring phase. Remember to file RCA and timeline in the incident tracker.
